newsitem.title: USA: Liberty, Prebon to acquire 49 pct of CBOT's CBB.
newsitem.headline: Liberty, Prebon to acquire 49 pct of CBOT's CBB.

text.p: Brokerage firms Liberty Brokerage Investment Corp and Prebon Yamane (USA) Inc will acquire 49 percent of the Chicago Board of Trade's electronic trading system, the Chicago Board Brokerage (CBB), the firms and the exchange announced Thursday.
The CBB will allow CBOT members and member firms to trade cash U.S. government securities.
Liberty and Prebon have established Hudson Holdings LLC to acquire the stake in CBB, which the CBOT began developing in 1992.

Liberty, a consortium of about a half-dozen primary dealers, and Prebon, the U.S. arm of London-based Fulton Prebon Group, said Hudson would develop the electronic trading system for all CBB products.
"There is a linkage among markets, among products, that attract us," Edwin Payne, CEO and president of Liberty, said at a news conference.

CBB, which received approval from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in December 1995, is expected to begin offering repos and U.S. Treasury bonds, notes and bills by mid-1997, CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said.

However, CBOT members must vote on the CBB alliance. Members must approve the purchase price of the joint venture, which Arbor refused to discuss. CBOT members, who currently have an option to purchase 100 percent of CBB from the exchange, will also be asked to agree to reduce that option to a 51 percent stake, he said.

Arbor said the CBB may eventually list Eurodollar derivatives, including back-month exchange-for-physicals (EFPs). EFPs allow a buyer or seller of a cash commodity to sell or buy an equivalent amount of futures out of the pit.

Liberty and Prebon at one time heavily used back-month Eurodollar EFPs at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange to trade TED spreads, which are trades between U.S. Treasuries and Eurodollar futures. The CME banned back-month Euro EFPs in late 1994.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission last month approved the CBOT as a contract market in options on Eurodollar futures. Earlier in the year, the CBOT won regulatory approval to list Eurodollar futures contracts.

"It's very possible down the line that our menu of products will include synthetic TED spreads," Arbor said, adding that the CBOT had been negotiating with Liberty and Prebon before the CME's ban on some ex-pit Euro contracts.

CBOT, Liberty and Prebon officials emphasized that trades on CBB, which will be cleared and settled by the Clearing Corporation for Options and Securities (CCOS), will reduce costs for all participants.
CCOS is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Board of Trade Clearing Corp, the CBOT's independent clearinghouse.

Liberty, which has about 500 employees worldwide, and Prebon, which has a total of 1,100 brokers around the world, also said their CBB alliance would not undermine the wholesale or primary dealer market.

"We don't see this as a vehicle for dismantling the wholesale markets," said David Rutter, managing director of Prebon Yamane (USA) Inc. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
